articleBody:
Before you buy lumber or pick out flooring for your basement remodel, run through this practical pre-construction checklist to confirm your space is ready for framing and code compliance.

- [ ] Measure ceiling clearance to the lowest duct or beam — Confirms your finished ceiling will meet local residential height codes.
- [ ] Tape plastic sheeting to bare concrete for 48 hours — Checks whether hidden moisture vapor is sweating through the slab before laying finished floors.
- [ ] Inspect foundation walls for active leaks or efflorescence — Ensures water infiltration issues are resolved before insulating and framing perimeter walls.
- [ ] Verify bedroom egress window net clear opening dimensions — Guarantees emergency rescue openings satisfy local fire and building life-safety rules.
- [ ] Locate the main water shutoff valve and cleanout plugs — Keeps emergency utility valves fully accessible through planned closets or service panels.
- [ ] Review electrical service panel for spare breaker spaces — Confirms your existing panel can supply new circuits for basement living areas and bathroom heat.
- [ ] Map out HVAC supply and return duct runs — Ensures balanced heating and cooling airflow across the newly enclosed rooms.
- [ ] Draft a dimensioned floor plan showing wall partitions — Needed for clear permit application reviews with your local building department.

How to use this checklist:
Walk your basement with this list in hand to identify hidden obstacles before ordering materials or finalizing your budget. Catching drainage issues, low clearances, or electrical limits early prevents change orders down the road.
